The Russia dossier establishes the large eastward reorientation of energy trade, but it does not add a new route-level dependency with sufficient canonical granularity beyond relationships already treated in the research layer.
The country dossier is historical and structural context rather than an actor-specific opportunity thesis.
State institutions and major sectors are analyzed at country level, without a new actor-specific control record that meets the Strategic Actors evidence standard.

EIA evidence establishes Russia's exceptional oil, gas and coal production/export scale, but the Resource Control Atlas requires controller-level legal ownership and operating-right evidence; a dedicated Gazprom/Rosneft/Transneft/Rosatom ownership pass is required before canonical insertion.
The publication is a long-run country dossier, not a bounded implemented policy case with a single design and outcome evaluation.
Current European security mechanisms are already represented by MT-CS-2026-09-20-EUR-RU-UA; the dossier adds historical and internal country context without changing the conflict-system state.
The dossier does not establish a new discrete technology capability signal or deployment-stage change.
